stories.title: Alternative explanation for the effect of myo-Inositol trispyrophosphate on normal human erythrocytes: 31P NMR studies
stories.description: myo-Inositol trispyrophosphate (ITPP) is an allosteric effector of haemoglobin in vitro and has been proposed as a therapeutic agent for diseases associated with tissue hypoxia. Its surmised action on erythrocytes (red blood cells; RBCs) requires transmembrane passage and intracellular binding to haemoglobin; however, direct evidence, of the kind provided by 31P NMR spectroscopy, for entry of ITPP into RBCs has been absent despite proposed clinical use of the compound. We tested transport by monitoring fresh human RBC suspensions exposed to ITPP using non-invasive 31P NMR spectroscopy over several hours. No intracellular ITPP was detected within the sensitivity limits of the method (~ 30 µM), and no evidence of significant accumulation was observed. Neither was there evidence of its hydrolysis in haemolysates. We conclude that ITPP does not permeate the normal human RBC membrane in measurable quantities under the conditions examined (and realistic in vivo ones). Consequently, the reported effects of ITPP when added to suspensions of RBCs, on haemoglobin oxygenation are unlikely to result from direct intracellular interaction with haemoglobin and are more plausibly ascribed to indirect effects arising from perturbation of ionic equilibria (Donnan effects) that affect intracellular pH and membrane potential.

stories.title: Green synthesis of multifunctional silver nanoparticles using Ocimum tenuiflorum L. inflorescence extract for potential antimicrobial and photocatalytic applications
stories.description: Green synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using plant-derived resources offers an alternative approach to conventional nanoparticle synthesis by utilizing naturally occurring phytoconstituents as reducing and stabilizing agents. In the present study, silver nanoparticles were synthesized using an aqueous inflorescence extract of Ocimum tenuiflorum L. (Tulsi) and systematically evaluated for their physicochemical characteristics and multifunctional properties. The synthesized Tulsi inflorescence-mediated AgNPs (TI-AgNPs) exhibited a characteristic surface plasmon resonance band at 428 nm, while TEM analysis showed nanoparticles within the 20–90 nm size range and XRD confirmed their crystalline nature. FTIR analysis indicated the involvement of hydroxyl, carbonyl, and other oxygen-containing functional groups in nanoparticle formation and stabilization. The TI-AgNPs demonstrated broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, with MIC values ranging from 8 to 64 µg/mL against the tested bacterial and fungal strains. DPPH assay showed concentration-dependent antioxidant activity, while the nanoparticles exhibited an IC₅₀ value of 634.71 µg/mL in HEK-293 cells. In addition, TI-AgNPs achieved 93.4% methylene blue removal within 60 min under sunlight irradiation. Overall, the findings demonstrate that O. tenuiflorum L inflorescence can serve as a plant-based source for the synthesis of multifunctional AgNPs with antimicrobial, antioxidant, and dye-removal properties, supporting their further investigation for potential biomedical and environmental applications.
